title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 1: Enter the Bio-Age
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 1 'Enter the Bio-Age': CJP's survey of the biosciences and biotechnologies (organ transplants, gene therapy, cloning, stem cells, DNA) transforming society and the legal and ethical questions they raise for the judiciary
sub_topics: Medical marvels and the body's rejection problem (transplants; Christian Barnard's first heart transplant)
The rise of biological technologies and 'healing miracles via the biosciences'
DNA in the courtroom — People v. Vallejo and Tijing v. Court of Appeals
Emerging ethical and legal issues: cloning, genetic engineering, patents on life
signature_phrases: unprecedented rise, expansion and pervasiveness of biological technologies

stances.claim: The biosciences and biotechnologies are ushering in a 'bio-age' that will test the law and the judiciary as profoundly as the information age did.

notable_anecdotes: He opens with Dr. Christian Barnard's first successful heart transplant and a Filipino senator's liver transplant from his son.
target_audience: general readers interested in science and law
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 1, 'Enter the Bio-Age,' surveys the biosciences and biotechnologies — organ transplants (opening with Christian Barnard's first heart transplant), gene therapy, cloning, stem cells, and DNA — transforming society, and the legal and ethical questions they pose for the judiciary. CJP touches on DNA evidence (People v. Vallejo, Tijing v. Court of Appeals) and intellectual property (RA 8293), arguing the incoming 'bio-age' will test the law as profoundly as the information age.
